newsitem.title: USA: Barnes sees record year in sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Barnes sees record year in sales, profits.

text.p: Barnes Group Inc said Thursday that it is off to a strong start for the year after reporting higher first quarter earnings and forecast that 1997 will be another year of record sales and profits.
The company earlier reported first quarter earnings per share of $0.50, up from $0.34 a year ago. These results were adjusted for a three-for-one stock split, effective in April, 1997.
Barnes said the strong quarter was due to continued profit growth in each of its three businesses, particularly Barnes Aerospace and Bowman Distribution.
"We're especially pleased with the excellent year-over-year progress made in improving advanced fabrications," company president Theodore Martin said.
Although total sales for its Bowman business in the first quarter were flat compared to a year ago, operating income was significantly higher.
Bowman continued to make solid progress in reducing operating costs and improving productivity, Barnes said.

Also contributing to Bowman's year-over-year profit improvement was an $0.8 million pretax charge, part of a $1.3 million company charge, covering a workforce reduction at Bowman taken in the first quarter of 1996.

Barnes Aerospace also showed significant year-over-year gains in sales and profits, and orders continue to be strong, Martin said. The group's precision machining unit continued to make excellent gains in penetrating the market for new generation aircraft engines, increasing its year-over-year order rate by 33 percent in the first quarter," Martin said.
"Sharp gains in sales and profits also continued at our aerospace engine overhaul and repair unit, due largely to expanded airline business, and at our advanced fabrications unit," he added.
